The propose projection was a LIST, and a list is the medium admitting it does
not know. Six surfaces re-derived the answer from len(survivors), and the
copies disagreed at the position where it costs most: render_at's
single-survivor arm destructured (survivor, _r) and DROPPED the Reason while
its tie arm two lines below carried one per candidate — the medium showing its
reasoning when unsure and withholding it where a developer is likeliest to
accept on faith.

Proposal({verdict, rejected}) over VFill(Node, Reason) | VAsk(Divergence,
[(Node, Reason)]) | VNone makes that drop unsayable: the constructor holds no
fill without its Why. Rejections sit beside the verdict rather than inside it,
since a lone survivor coexists with row-refused names and a refusal teaches
either way. Five re-derivations became reads; the sixth, teach_synthesize, had
zero callers — `mentl query src/mentl.mn unreferenced` named it — so it was
deleted rather than ported.

And the tie stopped saying the same sentence. Every tie ended in "one more
constraint (a refinement, a type, an example) collapses it": identical words at
every position, a placeholder wearing a teaching voice. Divergence classifies
what actually separates the survivors and speaks in that arm's own vocabulary,
in a stated precedence — ROW first (a capability difference changes what the
program may DO, read from the env entry the enumerator admitted each candidate
through, compared by mutual subsumption), then DENOTATION (a zero-arg call
followed to its callee's body, so pure_seven(), calm_seven() and the literal 7
are one value with three names), then VALUE (carrying the domain the seeder
already read), then SHAPE. The precedence is a judgment and is recorded as one:
a same-denotation tie is a MEANING tie at the intent altitude, not the free
form-space tie of the fork/merge duality, because cost is blind to what a later
reader learns from a name.

Constructor identity is the value word. Every nullary TokenKind compiles to its
discriminant sentinel, and `==` is structural (type-dispatched at emit to i32.eq
for an ADT operand) since Law 2. `at` only compares against nullary kind literals,
so `kind_eq(a, b) = a == b` — the kernel proves variant identity; the comparison
reads it. The 66-arm hand-rolled match was the incorrect re-derivation.

Seed compiles it to `(local.get $a)(local.get $b)(i32.eq)`; census holds at 173;
pass-2 P_UnexpectedToken 12387 -> 12058. The residual is non-uniform nullary
representation (a lexer-produced kind and a literal kind of the same constructor
differ in value-word — boxed vs sentinel), the named next gate.

perennials/2dc1ff1:
The sheet is a plan, and a guild is a vertical idea: the layers the guide
stacks results by are heights, and the one drawing she has could not show
them. Elevation is the second projection of the same yard, behind a toggle
on the sheet: a ground line, a height rule, and every placed plant standing
at the height our data gives it, in the shape of its recorded layer.

Size is a claim in this view, so only measurements make one. A plant with
no height in our data draws no figure: it stands on the line as the same
mark it is on the sheet, present and unmeasured, and the coverage line
counts how many stand that way. Shapes are the layer's, never the plant's;
there is no open dataset of species silhouettes for 8,800 plants, and
inventing one per plant would be the false-confidence trap in a new
dimension. A plant with no recorded layer wears the plain column, never a
tree's crown.

Her lane reaches the vertical too. A height she types on the panel stands
a figure up in her ink, by the same bargain as everywhere: the record's
value is never overwritten, hers counts exactly where the record is silent,
and only what parses as a measurement moves the drawing. "2 m", "250 cm"
and "6 ft" all do; "taller than the shed" stays on the page and off the
scale. The selected panel now offers the height blank, because the moment
she is looking at an unmeasured mark is the moment she knows the answer.

The vocabulary is borrowed on purpose. Marks, witness rings, show rings,
bloom fills and hatching come from the sheet unchanged; vines climb dashed
and roots reach below the line, as the guild spine already draws them, and
the below-ground wash is the spine's. The elevation is read-only: a tap
selects, and the tools stay with the paper.
bits/2d2fbe9:
A title strip, a real timeline, a dock that never changes shape, and
guidance you can read.

The title strip is laid over the top of the stage rather than above it.
With a title row, a timeline row and a dock all taking their own height, a
9:16 stage on a 390x844 phone comes out about 337px wide; laying the title
over it gives 48px of that back. It also gives a bit a name you can see
and change in place. Every bit was called "untitled bit" and renaming was
a system prompt on the list.

The timeline is its own full-width row: the waveform, the beat ticks the
onset grid already found, a playhead you can see and grab, and the time as
"0:04 / 0:12". It was 74px wide on a 390px phone with an invisible range
input over it and no duration anywhere. The moving parts are painted
through refs, so scrubbing and playback still cost no renders.

The dock is undo, redo, record, play, tools, always in that order. Redo
was three taps deep in the tools panel while undo sat on the bar.

Guidance moved into the banner over the top of the stage, at 15px. It was
13px along the bottom, where the puppets and the cancel pill covered it.
The walkthrough's "no instructive text under 15px" gap is closed; two
remain, both waiting on the halo in M4.

Also: rendering is cancellable and shows its progress on the stage instead
of inside a panel you can close; a short landscape window says to turn the
phone rather than squashing the stage into a postage stamp; waveform peaks
are a new pure engine function with its own tests.

Verified by eye as well as by assertion: the playhead was clipped in half
at either end of the track until the handle moved out of the clipping
layer, and the banner and the title strip were stacked on top of each
other until the banner learned where the strip ends.

97 unit tests, 21 of 23 walkthrough checks, typecheck, lint, build and
budget green.
